# gtk4's datepicker override writes a `#cal` in a library body, and main's
# own `#cal` is what `c.cal` names: it is null until main renders it, on every
# target. testdata/test_ref_owner_library.txtar is the gtk4 code.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

output {
    go {
        bubbletea
        fyne
        gtk4
    }
    kotlin {
        android
    }
    none {
        html
    }
}

component main node {
    var shown = false
    vbox {
        datepicker
        button #t(text="t", @click { shown = !shown })
        if shown {
            text #cal(value="c")
        }
    }
}

func testCal(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.cal == null)
    c.t.click()
    t.assert(c.cal != null)
    c.t.click()
    t.assert(c.cal == null)
}

window {
    main
}
